minutes.headline: Select Board suspended Mickey Shay's liquor license five days and called a special town meeting on solar power purchase.
minutes.summary: The board heard a water commissioners update and a police chief reminder on animal control, then took up a regional hazard mitigation plan. It held a liquor license hearing, found a violation and set a five-day suspension. It read the town manager's evaluation, moved to hold a special town meeting on the solar power purchase agreement, and made annual appointments.

what_happened.line: The Select Board found a violation at Mickey Shay's and recommended a five-day license suspension, June 27 through July 1.
The board moved to hold a special town meeting to bring the solar power purchase agreement to voters; the town manager is to present a date next week.
A motion was made to adopt the 2015 update of the regional natural hazard mitigation plan; the vote was not audible in the recording.
The board made its annual appointments and ratified the town manager's appointments as read.
The board agreed to work on a flag policy and to schedule a goal-setting workshop that would take up a whole meeting.

why_it_matters: The solar power purchase agreement is headed to a special town meeting, so residents will be asked to vote on a long-term electricity arrangement that can affect town energy costs.
The hazard mitigation plan is the kind of document that can bear on eligibility for outside emergency and mitigation funding, so the unrecorded vote outcome is worth confirming.
watch_next: The town manager's proposed special town meeting date, due at the board's next weekly meeting.
The suspension window of June 27 through July 1 and the paperwork to the licensee.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main votes and decisions, and most differences are caption misreadings of names and figures. The main gap is that our minutes record the 5-day suspension as a "recommend" vote, while the official minutes record it as a vote to issue the suspension. The official minutes also disagree with our minutes on several change-order figures, which should be checked.
